# Temple Scroll Column 3 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 3 | **Condition:** Heavily damaged; festival calendar fragments

---

**3:1** [...] the-festival [...] in-the-first month [...]

**3:2** [...] on the-fourteenth day of-the-month [...]

**3:3** [...] between the-evenings [...] the-Passover to-the-LORD [...]

**3:4** [...] and-you-shall-eat it [...] in-the-place which [I-shall-choose ...]

**3:5** [...] unleavened-bread [...] seven days you-shall-eat [...]

**3:6** [...] and-on-the-first day a-holy convocation [...]

**3:7** [...] all work of-labor you-shall-not do [...]

**3:8** [...] and-you-shall-bring-near an-offering-by-fire to-the-LORD [...]

**3:9** [...] seven days [...] unleavened-bread [...]

**3:10** [...] and-on-the-seventh day a-holy convocation to-the-LORD [...]

---

*EMET notes: Column 3 is heavily damaged but preserves the beginning of the festival calendar, starting with Passover and Unleavened Bread (cf. Lev 23:5-8, Num 28:16-25). God continues speaking in the first person. The text closely parallels the Pentateuchal festival legislation but reformulates it as direct divine speech. "Between the evenings" (bein ha-'arbayim) is preserved literally as in Exodus 12:6.*
